data.theme: Entrepreneurial Motivation and Career Intentions in Engineering
data.definition: The identification and assessment of motivational factors influencing engineering students' entrepreneurial intentions and career trajectories. This includes examining the roles of personal interests, managerial motives, and perceived career benefits in shaping entrepreneurial behavior.

data.theme: Writing Attitudes and Academic Performance in Engineering
data.definition: The evaluation of engineering students' attitudes toward writing, including emotional responses (e.g., apprehension) and cognitive engagement, and their relationship to academic success and career development. This theme also encompasses the validation of survey instruments used to measure these attitudes.

The assessment and development of leadership-related competencies in engineering students, including team motivation, ethical decision-making, and innovative change management. This theme focuses on both the identification of these competencies and the evaluation of educational programs designed to cultivate them.

The measurement of self-efficacy among biomedical engineering students, particularly their confidence in addressing clinical problems, proposing solutions, and engaging in interdisciplinary collaborations. This theme emphasizes the clinical relevance of self-efficacy and its role in professional development.

data.theme: Educational Assessment Policy and Institutional Impact
data.definition: The use of validated assessment instruments to inform institutional policies, educational research, and broader policy decisions in engineering education. This theme explores how assessment outcomes drive curriculum development, accreditation processes, and systemic improvements in engineering programs.
